A.note: Warm, readable aerial of the fortified town with a muzzle flash and drifting smoke. The ground texture is better than in B, with grainy terrain and some variation. The buildings are uniform orange blocks that look like game pieces. The ships are tiny specks and the smoke is soft and sprite-like.

B.note: Same composition as A, but the ground is flatter and smoother, with a plain beige plane in the town area and less terrain texture. The buildings look like cardboard models. The sea is nicer, with an added headland, but overall it reads as a diorama.

C.note: Dramatic night shot with a silhouetted ridge, glowing floating batteries and reflections on the water. The mood and lighting are the strongest of the three. The batteries are simple glowing boxes and the water is a bit noisy. The frame is dark and does not show the fortified town.

why: C has the strongest cinematic lighting and mood and the least toy look, while A has richer ground texture than B, whose flat ground makes it read as a diorama.
top_fix_for_best: Give the floating batteries real ship detail (sloped timber sides, rigging, gun ports, masts and hull textures), add a lit town and fortress on the shore, and make the muzzle flashes and smoke volumetric so the shot reads as a battle.
